Class SubscriptionService

java.lang.Object
york.studentevents.subscriptions.SubscriptionService
public class SubscriptionService extends Object
Application service coordinating event subscriptions and the notifications sent to subscribers.

Sits over the ISubscriptionRepository (the durable record of who subscribes to which event) and the Observer pattern, which delivers notifications. It records and reconciles subscriptions, reports whether a user is subscribed, and publishes a NotificationType to an event's subscribers by populating an EventNotificationService from the stored records.

A user holds at most one subscription per event. Explicit subscriptions are sticky: registration never overwrites one and deregistration never removes one; only an explicit unsubscribe does.

Note that no validation is performed against the user or event IDs passed in. That logic is delegated to the StudentEventService which owns the instance of SubscriptionService.

  • Method Details

    • subscribe

      public void subscribe(UUID userId, UUID eventId, ISubscription.SubscriptionSource reason)
      Subscribes a User to a given Event, reconciling the request with any subscription the user already holds for the event. A user holds at most one subscription per event.

      A ISubscription.SubscriptionSource.REGISTRATION request creates a registration-based subscription only when the user has none. It never disturbs an existing subscription, so an explicit subscription stays sticky and takes precedence.

      A ISubscription.SubscriptionSource.EXPLICIT request ensures an explicit, sticky subscription: a registration-based subscription is upgraded to explicit so that it survives a later deregistration, and subscribing explicitly when already explicitly subscribed fails.

      Note that, due to the nature of SubscriptionService, no validation is performed against the IDs provided. This logic should be delegated to the StudentEventService which owns the instance of SubscriptionService.

      Parameters:
      userId - The user's ID
      eventId - The event's ID
      reason - The reason why the subscription is being created.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if reason is ISubscription.SubscriptionSource.EXPLICIT and the user is already explicitly subscribed to the event.
      See Also:
      • ISubscription.SubscriptionSource

    • unsubscribe

      public void unsubscribe(UUID userId, UUID eventId, ISubscription.SubscriptionSource reason)
      Removes a User's subscription to a given Event, with the effect depending on why the unsubscription is requested. A user holds at most one subscription per event.

      A ISubscription.SubscriptionSource.REGISTRATION request (a deregistration) removes only a registration-based subscription. An explicit subscription is left untouched, and if no matching subscription exists the state is simply left unaffected: this is not an error.

      A ISubscription.SubscriptionSource.EXPLICIT request (an explicit unsubscription) removes the user's subscription regardless of how it was created.

      Note that, due to the nature of SubscriptionService, no validation is performed against the IDs provided. This logic should be delegated to the StudentEventService which owns the instance of SubscriptionService.

      Parameters:
      userId - The user's ID
      eventId - The event's ID
      reason - The reason why the subscription is being removed.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if reason is ISubscription.SubscriptionSource.EXPLICIT and the user is not subscribed to the event.
      See Also:
      • ISubscription.SubscriptionSource

    • publish

      public void publish(UUID eventId, NotificationType reason)
      Publish a notification to the subscribers of an event.

      Creates an instance of EventNotificationService, which is used to notify a UserEventObserver of each User subscribed to the Event.

      Note that, due to the nature of SubscriptionService, no validation is performed to check whether an Event with the given ID exists; this logic should be delegated to the StudentEventService which owns the instance of SubscriptionService.

      Parameters:
      eventId - The event about which to publish a notification.
      reason - The reason for the notification
      See Also:
      • NotificationType
      • EventNotificationService
